output.scope: External means not resolved to a module or namespace in this scanned import root. Names include standard-library and third-party imports; they are not distribution names or installation requirements. Routes follow explicit local edges only and do not establish execution. Conditions, function bodies, dynamic targets, implicit package startup and installed packages are not simulated. Absence of a route does not prove an import unused. Review issues, cycles, dynamic calls and skips.
output.collection_scope: Complete means collection finished within the stated budgets, not that runtime imports are known. Hidden and conventional dependency directories, symlinks and nonregular files are skipped. Explicit AST imports only; parse issues and dynamic calls remain visible. Use a stable source tree. These are input-size limits, not CPU, memory or elapsed-time guarantees.

limits: Saved evidence only; no new request or retry was made.

Saved header hints only; no network, waiting, scheduling or retries.
An elapsed hint does not establish health or permission to retry.
Delay-seconds start at recorded receipt; HTTP dates use the local recorded clock.
Clock skew and transit/cache age are not corrected or inferred.
Only IMF-fixdate dates are supported; malformed/obsolete values remain unknown.
Old reports without retry_after cannot establish header absence.
Status context alone does not establish the cause or scope of a failure.

result.scope: Freshness metadata only; not permission to store or reuse a response. Request directives, Vary matching, authorization, cache keys and stale extensions are not evaluated. No conditional request is sent.
